record.original_question: Characterize exactly which abstract polytopes P have monodromy group Mon(P) that is a string C-group, so that the minimal regular cover obtained from Mon(P) is itself polytopal.

evidence.quote: Problem 4. Give a characterization of the polytopes P such that Mon(P) is a string C-group.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Setup. An abstract polytope of rank n is a partially ordered set P of "faces", with a unique minimum face and a unique maximum face, in which every maximal chain (flag) contains exactly n+2 elements, P is strongly flag-connected, and the diamond condition holds: whenever F < G are faces with rank(G) − rank(F) = 2, there are exactly two faces H with F < H < G. For each i ∈ {0, 1, …, n−1} and each flag Φ of P, there is a unique flag Φ^i differing from Φ only in the face of rank i. The monodromy group Mon(P) is the subgroup of the symmetric group on the set F(P) of flags generated by the permutations σ_0, σ_1, …, σ_{n−1} defined by σ_i(Φ) = Φ^i.

A string C-group of rank n is a pair (G, {ρ_0, …, ρ_{n−1}}) where G is a group generated by involutions ρ_0, …, ρ_{n−1} that satisfy the string condition (ρ_i ρ_j)^2 = 1 whenever |i − j| ≥ 2 and the intersection condition ⟨ρ_i : i ∈ I⟩ ∩ ⟨ρ_i : i ∈ J⟩ = ⟨ρ_i : i ∈ I ∩ J⟩ for all I, J ⊆ {0, …, n−1}. When Mon(P) (with its distinguished generators σ_0, …, σ_{n−1}) is a string C-group, the abstract regular polytope associated with Mon(P) is the (unique) minimal regular cover of P; when Mon(P) fails the intersection condition, this construction does not yield a polytope.

Problem. Give a complete characterization of those abstract polytopes P for which Mon(P), with its distinguished generators σ_0, …, σ_{n−1}, is a string C-group (equivalently, for which the minimal regular cover of P obtained from Mon(P) is itself an abstract polytope).
artifact.status_search_result: The problem remains an active area of investigation. While Mon(P) is always a string C-group when P has rank ≤ 3, examples such as the tomotope show this fails for rank ≥ 4, and determining which polytopes are "C-connected" (i.e., have monodromy group satisfying the intersection condition) is described in the literature as an ongoing open research direction with no general characterization available.

status_evidence.title: Monodromy group - Polytope Wiki
status_evidence.snippet: The tomotope provided the first well-understood example of an abstract 4-polytope whose connection (monodromy) group is not a string C-group; if the connection group is a string C-group, the polytope has a unique minimal regular cover.
status_evidence.claim: Mon(P) being a string C-group is not automatic in rank ≥ 4, and identifying when it holds is open.

status_evidence.title: Regular Covers and Monodromy Groups of Abstract Polytopes (Monson)
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses cases in which the monodromy group of an abstract polytope yields a polytopal minimal regular cover, with examples and obstructions.
status_evidence.claim: Characterization of when Mon(P) is a string C-group remains an active research question.
